raw_response:
I’m an old hand at this now. On my 2 mu, I still keep the wheat-maize rotation. That way the land does not sit empty, and even if one crop does poorly, the other can still bring something back. I cannot take big risks. What I do is mostly what has worked on my fields before. Wheat needs a steady hand, a few waterings from the well, and enough fertilizer so it does not turn yellow. Maize follows right after wheat, so there is no time for fancy work. We harvest wheat, clear the field fast, scratch the soil, and sow maize right away. Money matters, so I will not buy the most expensive seed or too much chemical, but I also do not dare cut fertilizer too hard because if yield falls, that hurts more than spending a little extra. Family labor is still the main thing for us, and if we get too busy at harvest and planting together, we may hire a little machine help.
